newsitem.title: UK: Rank sees operating profit growth in H2.
newsitem.headline: Rank sees operating profit growth in H2.

text.p: British leisure company Rank Group Plc said on Thursday that the growth in operating profit before exceptionals it had posted in the first half had been broadly maintained in the second half.
"In a year of transition, we are making good trading and strategic progress," chief executive Andrew Teare said in a trading update.
Among its divisions, Rank said film and entertainment services' video duplication volumes had grown by 16 percent in the 11 months ended November 30.
Overall, video profits increased strongly during the second half, helped by improved operating efficiency and by better capacity utilisation, Rank said.

The company said overall profit at its Hard Rock Cafe chain was higher, although operating profit at its "Rank" cafes was slightly lower than in 1995. Earlier this year, Rank bought the Hard Rock chain from joint founder Peter Morton, adding about 13 cafes and four franchises to the ones the company already owned.
Rank said it planned to speed up the chain's expansion beyond the 64 owned and franchised cafes it currently has.
Regarding other divisions, the company said the volume of holidays sold at its Holidays UK unit rose by over three percent in the 11-month period.
Rank said gaming turnover and profit was higher, with UK bingo admissions in line with 1995, with an average of five percent fewer clubs.

The company said revenues at its Rank Xerox venture with Xerox Corp rose by two percent in the nine months to September 30, although its participation profit slid three percent, excluding a first-quarter restructuring charge.
Rank's shares dropped 9.5p to 432.5 by 0900 GMT.
